items.body: The Detroit Red Wings will be without their No. 1 goaltender for the remainder of Tuesday's game. John Gibson did not come out for the second period against the Tampa Bay Lightning and was later ruled out by the Red Wings with a lower-body injury. Gibson, 33, has played 10 games for the Red Wings this season, owning a 3.37 goals-against average and a .860 save percentage. Though he has played the entirety of his last three games, he exited after the second period against the Vancouver Canucks on Oct. 22. The Pittsburgh native is in his second season with the Red Wings after spending the first 12 seasons of his career with the Anaheim Ducks.

This was Turcotte’s first time skating with the team since he was placed on injured reserve on October 10 with an undisclosed injury, although he has been skating on his own for the past several days. Adrian Kempe is day-to-day after sitting out Saturday’s 3-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres. Both Mats Zuccarello and Kevin Fiala remain on IR. Zuccarello is considered week-to-week with an upper-body injury, while Fiala has yet to play this season as he works back from the broken leg he suffered at the 2026 Winter Olympics, which required a second procedure over the summer. Los Angeles sits at 4-7-2 through 13 games, last in the Pacific Division with 10 points, after opening Peter Laviolette ’s first season behind the bench with six straight losses (0-4-2). Scoring has been the primary issue. The Kings’ 36 goals rank 28th in the league, and they are shooting 9.9 percent as a team (league average of 11.5 percent). Artemi Panarin leads the club with eight goals and 13 points, and no other King has more than three goals. Special teams haven’t helped either, with the power play converting at a middle of the pack 18.2 percent but the penalty kill sitting at a league worst 61.5 percent. The Kings are also playing their first season since longtime captain Anze Kopitar retired, which has left them thinner down the middle. That raises the stakes for Turcotte’s return. items.body: Forward passed Lowe for most games played in franchise history NEWARK, N.J. – Ryan Nugent-Hopkins felt the significance of his next game and the milestone it represents for the Edmonton Oilers when he saw his teammates Tuesday morning. There they were, all wearing T-shirts that depicted the Oilers forward with a mullet, smoking a cigarette, wearing a short-sleeved camo shirt, and with a tattoo on his arm. On the shirt were the words “1038 games Most Games Played as an Edmonton Oiler.” Nugent-Hopkins hit that mark when the Oilers played the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center on Tuesday. The 32-year-old forward, selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, passed Kevin Lowe, who played 1,037 games during his 15 seasons with Edmonton. They are the two to have played at least 1,000 games for the Oilers. "I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team," Nugent-Hopkins said Tuesday. "It really is a testament to a lot of these guys in this room, and not just the players but the staff, the trainers that have been here for my entire career." After showing him the T-shirts, the Oilers played him a video celebrating his career. "I feel the love," Nugent-Hopkins said. "Having a video that they shared with me was definitely special. To have experienced a lot of these games with a few of the guys in here, it's pretty special. I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team." items.body: Center has four points in 14 games this season; Seattle receives Wood in return Shane Wright was traded to the Nashville Predators by the Seattle Kraken for Matthew Wood on Sunday. Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. "I was surprised, but I was excited as well," Wright said Monday. "Really unbelievable city and organization. I'm excited to be here. "I think, for me, I always wanted a little more opportunity. I wanted to have more minutes. I wanted to play a bigger role, whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else. I was happy to do that, but I'm moving on from the situation and happy to be here. I'm still young, so I want to hopefully be here for a number of years, build something special here and be part of a winning culture and a winning group." The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. "For us, we just felt it made sense for quite a few reasons," Predators general manager Chris MacFarland said. "We're excited to add Shane. We feel he's a natural fit in the middle of the ice. We feel we've got a great opportunity for him to improve day by day. He'll be a better player in the spring than he is now, and he'll be a better player next fall than he is now. We hope the same for Matthew. This is one that you hope works out for both teams." The Predators (5-4-5) host the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; HHN, CARNHL, SCRIPPS, SN+).

Complications as a result of the surgery as well as some medications arose, which have impacted his energy, weight and speech. Francis added that Iginla has been tested and has met with numerous medical professionals for over a year to get a clearer idea of what the 49-year-old is dealing with. Iginla had hip replacement surgery earlier in retirement after sustaining plenty of impact in his NHL career, and medications that followed the complications of the surgery have impacted his energy, weight and speech, according to Sportsnet’s report. items.body: Team will honor late country legend on shoulder of new sweater design during warmups on Nov. 7 If you thought the Nashville Predators Hometown Remix jersey couldn’t get any more “honky-tonk,” think again. On Tuesday, the team unveiled a special Dolly Parton jersey patch that will be worn on sweaters during warmups before the team’s matchup against the St. Louis Blues on Saturday, Nov. 7 (1 p.m. ET; STLNHL, BN+, NHLN, SN+, SCRIPPS). Modeling the new addition to the jerseys was Predators legend Pekka Rinne , who spent his entire 15-year NHL career in Nashville. Rinne will wear the new patch to Bridgestone Arena on Tuesday, where he’ll participate in the ceremonial puck drop ahead of the team’s Hockey Fights Cancer Night matchup against the Carolina Hurricanes (8 p.m. ET; CARNHL, HHN, SN+, SCRIPPS). The patches feature a golden butterfly – one of Parton’s iconic symbols – to honor the “Queen of Country,” who died in August in Nashville. In addition to the patches, the warmup sweaters will have “Dolly” on the nameplates with each players’ number. After warmups, the jerseys will be signed and auctioned off through the Nashville Predators Foundation with proceeds benefiting Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library and the Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt. The Predators Foundation will also host a book drive during Hometown Remix games with donations going to the Imagination Library.

items.body: The Winnipeg Jets and Toronto Maple Leafs are both making adjustments to their rosters. The Jets announced on Tuesday that they had placed centre Brad Lambert on waivers. The decision comes after Lambert featured in 11 games for the Jets this season, notching one assist. Lambert was selected 30th overall by the Jets in the 2022 Draft and has tallied three goals and six assists in 42 games across four seasons. He has also played 173 games for the AHL Manitoba Moose, picking up 36 goals and 70 assists. As for the Leafs, there were no takers after placing forward Bo Groulx on waivers on Monday. The team announced that he would be reassigned to the AHL Toronto Marlies. Groulx now clears after a seven-game stint with the Leafs where he failed to record a point. Originally from Rouen, France, the 26-year-old forward was taken in the second round of the 2018 draft by the Anaheim Ducks. He managed 13 games with the Leafs last year but predominantly featured for the Marlies, where he racked up 52 points in 59 games.

items.body: CALGARY - For years, Jarome Iginla played through just about everything hockey could throw at him. Broken bones, bruises, bumps, slashes, playoff wars and the relentless punishment of more than 1,600 NHL games. Nothing seemed capable of keeping one of the toughest competitors in Calgary Flames history down for long. Now, the Hockey Hall of Famer is facing a battle far removed from the rink. “Unfortunately I have been battling some health issues,” said the 49-year-old from his home in Lake Country, B.C. “Some neurological issues. I’m not entirely sure what it is, it may be from metal toxins from reaction to the cobalt hip.” Iginla underwent hip replacement surgery a few years ago after a career spent absorbing the physical toll of professional hockey. Complications followed, along with medications that have affected his energy, weight and speech. There are concerns that the cobalt-chromium components used in some artificial hip implants can release metal ions and debris through wear or corrosion, potentially causing complications as they enter the bloodstream. He also had high mercury levels in his body and is working to get that down, while trying to determine if the cause is related to the cobalt poisoning. Iginla has spent well over a year getting tests and consulting with medical professionals in an ongoing effort to get answers about what is happening and how best to treat it. “I need more time to figure it all out, but I’m still hopeful that I will recover fully,” he said. That's the encouraging part. The rest remains a work in progress. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images A struggling center looks to be on his way back down to the minors, where a larger role awaits. On Tuesday, the Winnipeg Jets placed forward Brad Lambert on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. If Lambert clears waivers on Wednesday, he’ll become eligible to be assigned to the Jets’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Manitoba Moose. Lambert has been in the lineup for most of the first month of the 2026-27 season in Winnipeg, but, like the team around him, hasn’t done much. In 11 appearances, he has just one assist, that coming in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Chicago Blackhawks on Oct. 15. He has gone pointless in each of his previous five games, last dressing in the Jets lineup last Thursday, when the team lost a tough battle to the Tampa Bay Lightning , 5-4. The 22-year-old logged less than nine minutes of ice time in the defeat. Lambert has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:10 of ice time per game. There was belief that Lambert could see some considerable playing time with the Jets this season. He posted three goals and six points in 25 contests during the 2025-26 season, the most during a single campaign in his brief NHL tenure. However, the organization appears to believe his talent could be used in the AHL. In 42 games in the NHL, the former first-round pick has three goals and nine points. In 173 regular-season games in the AHL, Lambert has posted 36 goals and 70 assists for 106 points, with one assist in nine Calder Cup Playoff contests. The only player put on waivers on Monday was Toronto Maple Leafs forward Bo Groulx. He cleared and can now be sent down to the Leafs’ top farm team, the Toronto Marlies.

items.title: Weegar loves watching Russia play hockey, but says Europe may see it differently
items.body: MacKenzie Weegar says he enjoys watching Russia play in the top hockey tournaments. But the Canadian defenceman says Russia's return to international competition might be viewed differently by European players. "I know those (Russian) guys want to play in it really badly, but it's obviously a different time, and people have their views on it," Weegar said Tuesday before his Utah Mammoth played the Maple Leafs in Toronto. " But I've always loved seeing Russia in the Olympics and in those best-on-bests." The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week that the International Ice Hockey Federation must reinstate Russian teams, beginning with the world juniors, which start Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Russia and its ally Belarus had been barred from competition since Russia began its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The ruling has prompted a backlash from several European hockey federations. Sweden, Finland, Czechia and Latvia have said their national teams will not play Russia in international competition. Norway and Denmark have said they will not play Russia at the 2027 men’s world championship in Germany, while Austria opposes Russia’s return. "It's different for those countries out there, right? You don't really feel the impact out in North America," Weegar said. "They have their opinions on it, and so they should. "Hopefully they can solve those issues and get Russia back into it." In NHL locker rooms, some Swedish and Finnish players were reluctant to weigh in, leaving that to their respective federations. items.title: Oilers’ Howard out week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.summary: Howard was hurt when he was on the wrong end of a knee-on-knee hit from the Islanders’ Emil Heineman.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Peter Creveling-Imagn Images A young up-and-comer is going to miss an extended period of time. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock revealed that forward Isaac Howard is considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury. Babcock noted that Howard is doing better and seems optimistic that he’ll return sooner rather than later. “[Howard] is good,” Babcock said. “He’s going to be out a couple weeks, I think. But it’s nothing. It’s not a big deal.” Howard was hurt during Saturday night’s game between the Oilers and the New York Islanders . Early in the first period, Islanders forward Emil Heineman delivered a knee-on-knee hit to Howard in the neutral zone. Howard needed assistance getting off the ice. He returned to the Edmonton locker room and was later ruled out for the rest of the game, logging just 30 seconds of ice time. Heineman was given a five-minute major penalty for kneeing and a game misconduct. For Howard, who has played in all but two games for the Oilers so far this season, he will miss at least the remainder of the team’s road trip out East, which concludes on Tuesday night against the New Jersey Devils . Edmonton returns home on Thursday, taking on the Anaheim Duck s, beginning a four-game homestand. In just his second season with the Oilers, the 2025 Hobey Baker winner has produced a little bit on the offensive end. In 13 contests, he has scored a goal and three points, just a couple off matching his five-point performance from last season, where he dressed in 29 games. The Oilers (11-2-2) sit atop the Pacific Division, four points ahead of the Vegas Golden Knights .

items.title: Checking in on early returns of Maple Leafs’ go-to goalie Sergei Bobrovsky
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. Has it been worth it? Adam Vingan checks in on the early returns.
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs ’ decision to sign Sergei Bobrovsky for three years came with enormous risk. General manager John Chayka gambled that a goaltender — albeit one destined for the Hockey Hall of Fame — coming off the worst season of his career at 37 would rebound. At least to start the season, the worst-case scenario has come to pass. Sure, it’s a small sample size, but Bobrovsky has allowed at least three goals in nine of his 10 starts, already leading to questions about whether the Maple Leafs should adjust his workload. “We brought (Bobrovsky) in to be there when the pressure ramps up and we need a rock back there,” Chayka told reporters . Unfortunately, Bobrovsky has yet to harden into that rock. His .809 save percentage on slot shots ranks 39th out of 53 goaltenders who have appeared in at least five games this season. It is an improvement from the .789 he posted last season with the Florida Panthers that ranked 64th among 66 qualified goaltenders (minimum 20 games played). But more is expected from the ninth-highest-paid goaltender in that group. (Across Florida’s consecutive Stanley Cup-winning seasons in 2023-24 and 2024-25, Bobrovsky recorded an .839 slot save percentage.) “I don’t try to overthink, I try to stay just with the moment and try to stop the next shot,” Bobrovsky told reporters . “It is a new team. It’s not only me, lots of new pieces, new system, new guys, so we just build the chemistry, build the belief.” All athletes, even those as finely tuned as Bobrovsky, eventually lose their sharpness. In Bobrovsky’s case, his reflexes appear to have slowed. Opponents have been picking on Bobrovsky’s glove hand, which seems to have lost some of its zip. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Calgary Flames started the season with a four-game losing streak that saw them sink to a minus-19 goal differential while looking completely uncompetitive. Since then, a team that entered the year tabbed as one of the favorites to finish with the worst record in the NHL and have the best odds at the number one overall pick in the 2027 NHL Draft next June has gone 7-4-0 and moved to just one point out of a playoff spot as solid goaltending and quality play from a defense deep with young talent has powered some surprising success. On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , host Tyler Yaremchuk and co-host and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discussed the Flames’ hot run as it relates to their interest in getting a top talent at the top of the draft this season. Tyler Yaremchuk : One of the more surprising results last night—although if you were Carter Hutton and you nailed it in the betting segment, the Flames beating the San Jose Sharks last night. items.body: Register Login Matthew Poitras Suffered Face Injury By Marcus Antonelli | at November 3, 2026 10:43 am Matthew Poitras is not present at Bruins practice, according to Scott McLaughlin of WEEI . The reasoning behind that regards a hit he sustained in the Bruins’ 3-2 shootout win over the reigning Western Conference Champion Vegas Golden Knights. Poitras, while carrying the puck through the neutral zone, funneled a cross-ice pass as he skated near the benches. Braeden Bowman , who was parallel to the young center, made contact with his head, using his elbow to knock down Poitras at 2:49 of the second period. Poitras was able to will himself off the ice and returned with a full bubble shield, but did not play another shift. Poitras ended his night with 3:13 of ice time. Sean Kuraly skated on the fourth line at Bruins practice. Marco Sturm did not provide a postgame update. Bowman received a five-minute major and a game misconduct. According to Frank Seravalli , Bowman has not received any more discipline. As he described it, Bowman made sure his elbow was close to his body; as a result, this is not viewed as elbowing, per Seravalli. Along with the reverse angle showing Poitras skating into Bowman, his head is not ‘deemed to be the principal point of contact.’ Poitras has been a key player for the Bruins this season. The 22-year-old, who has 7 points in 12 NHL games, has gotten more leeway compared to his past two years under the organization, which saw much more time in the AHL with the Providence Bruins. Playing fourth-line minutes at that scoring clip, Poitras has been a major part of the Bruins’ youth movement. He’s within the top-10 scorers on Boston, and is 10th in the entire NHL in scoring per 60 minutes, with 3.78, just playing under 10 minutes of average ice time.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources A new wrinkle in the saga following an international court’s controversial decision. After a cabinet meeting on Monday, Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis announced that the country will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to compete in the upcoming IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship, set to take place in Ostrava from Jan. 8-16. Babis cited the ongoing war in Ukraine as a major reason the country wouldn’t allow Russia to play in the event. “It doesn’t make sense to me as long as the war in Ukraine continues,” Babis said in his translated remarks. “It would create the impression that war and killing are normal, which we reject.” The announcement comes after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Friday that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation can immediately participate in International Ice Hockey Federation tournaments, ending a ban instituted after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Babis added that he believes in the separation of politics and athletics, but the CAS’ decision waives that notion. “I agree that politics should not interfere with sports, but this decision brings politics into it.” In 2023, Czechia instituted a suspension of granting visas to Russian national teams. Systems are important in hockey, particularly in the NHL. It’s the blueprint of how a team plays. But the reason a team plays the way it does is just as important. It is necessary to have a system and an investment in the players in equal measure. That’s what you see from good teams at any level. If a coach can get his players to play to the best of their ability, the chosen system will work better. If you can get 75 percent of your players at their best, you are going to probably have success. You're going to win. He returned to the Marlies for the 2026 Calder Cup playoffs, where he scored eight goals and 14 points in 23 games, helping the organization win a championship. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources After much anticipation (and many leaks), the NHL and Fanatics, its official uniform partner, finally unveiled the Hometown Remix line of speciality jerseys on Monday. As a spiritual successor to the two Reverse Retro programs the league debuted in collaboration with Adidas in recent years, the Hometown Remix line allows each of the NHL’s 32 teams to introduce new designs with distinct ties to their city and hockey community. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen Brashear-Imagn Images An experienced center is expected to head back to the minors. On Monday, the Toronto Maple Leafs placed forward Bo Groulx on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. If Groulx clears waivers on Tuesday, he can be assigned to the Maple Leafs’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Toronto Marlies. Groulx has been with the Leafs since the onset of the 2026-27 season, but has only played sparingly, having spent most of the first month as a healthy scratch. He was last in the lineup last Thursday, when Toronto fell to the Seattle Kraken , 5-4. In that contest, Groulx logged 6:23 of ice time, putting one shot on goal. In seven appearances thus far, the 26-year-old has yet to register a point. He has a plus/minus of +1 while averaging a hair over eight minutes of ice time per game. The beginning of the new season comes after he played 13 games for the Leafs last year, his first NHL experience in two years, posting three goals and five points. Groulx proved to be a key piece in the Marlies’ success last year. Along with scoring a career-high 28 goals and 52 points in 59 regular-season games, the Rouen, France native posted eight goals and 14 points in 23 playoff contests, helping the Marlies win the franchise’s second Calder Cup . In 85 games in the NHL, Groulx has notched four goals and six assists for 10 points. He’s in the second season of a two-year contract, which he signed with the Leafs in July 2025. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images After Friday’s stunning news that star winger Nikita Kucherov has requested a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning , we’ve gotten statements from Lightning general manager Julien Brisebois and head coach Jon Cooper on the matter. Now, we finally got to hear from the man at the center of the news. Kucherov held a media scrum on Monday and answered questions about his trade request for the first time, addressing the reasoning behind his decision. “It was never about the money for me,” Kucherov told reporters. “It was more about poor communication and respect. Over the last four months, we only have had two conversations. Julian, in the end, made it clear that I’m free to walk on July 1st.” From his comments, it seems that Kucherov felt he hasn’t received the treatment befitting Tampa Bay’s all-time scoring leader that has won two Stanley Cups and two Hart Trophies with the Lightning. Kucherov, 33, is in the final season of an eight-year, $76 million contract with Tampa Bay. He’s made it clear he does not plan to re-sign with the Lightning, but stated on Monday that he will continue to give his full effort while he remains on the team. “For now, I’m part of this team, and I will do anything I can to help my teammates win,” Kucherov said. items.summary: Speaking with reporters after the Tampa Bay Lightning’s Monday practice, Kucherov explained that his decision to request a trade from the only NHL team he’s known came down to a matter of “poor communication and respect.”
items.body: Nikita Kucherov is finally clearing the air following his shock trade request. Speaking with reporters after the Tampa Bay Lightning 's Monday practice, Kucherov explained that his decision to request a trade from the only NHL team he's known came down to a matter of "poor communication and respect." "It was never about the money for me, more about poor communication and respect," Kucherov said, head down and surrounded by reporters. "Over the last four months, we only have had two conversations. And (Lightning general manager) Julien (BriseBois), in the end, made it clear that I'm free to walk on July 1." Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Friday that Kucherov had informed his teammates and the Lightning organization that he would not be re-signing in Tampa Bay when his contract runs out at the end of the season and that he would like to be traded. Kucherov, playing in the final year of an eight-year, $76-million deal, reportedly hadn't made progress with the organization on an extension, and meetings with BriseBois were few and far between. When asked about whether he sees himself in Tampa beyond this season, Kucherov simply stated: "I made my request." Following the report that Kucherov had submitted a trade request, the Lightning released a statement saying they would not be trading the superstar. "We are aware of the media reports regarding the future of Nikita Kucherov with the Lightning," Brisebois said in a statement. "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita." For now, Kucherov appears intent on helping the team while still wearing a Lightning sweater, saying, "For now I'm part of this team, and I will do anything I can to help my teammates win." items.body: It'll be Sergei Bobrovsky between the pipes on Tuesday for the Toronto Maple Leafs . Despite recent struggles, the prized free-agent addition will start against the Utah Mammoth, head coach Jim Hiller told reporters on Monday. Bobrovsky allowed five goals in his most recent start Thursday against the Seattle Kraken, including the game-winner in the final minute on a shot from the point. On the season, the Russian has a 3-5-2 record with an .885 save percentage and 3.29 goals-against average. "Just one hell of a goalie, the way he works day in and day out," Stolarz said of Bobrovsky Monday. items.body: Cammi Granato played with Cindy Curley for the United States women's hockey team in 1990, when they won silver at the inaugural IIHF Women's World Championship. Granato also won gold with the U.S. at the 1998 Nagano Olympics, the first to feature women's hockey, and silver at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics. Granato was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2010, one of the first women to receive that honor, and was assistant general manager for the Vancouver Canucks from 2022-26. Now senior advisor for amateur scouting for the Canucks, Granato shares her thoughts on Curley, who will be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, in a special testimonial. I'm thrilled that Cindy Curley is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. She's the player who I always thought deserved to be in. When she played and was dominating her sport, there wasn't a lot of emphasis on women's hockey in the U.S. I learned about her by happenstance. I played hockey with the boys in Chicago until I was 17 and thought it may be the end of the road for me in hockey because the boys were turning into men. My mom was trying to get me into other sports, knowing that there wasn’t much room for me in men's hockey, and because we didn't know there was women's hockey out east. A father on one of the boys' teams that we were playing gave my mom a pamphlet from Providence College where Cindy was playing. It had their scoring statistics, and she was at the top of the list and dominating the score sheet. When I got that pamphlet, Cindy instantly became my first female hockey idol. items.body: Pioneering forward, Providence College legend won silver medal with U.S. three times The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Patrice Bergeron , Cindy Curley, Carey Price , Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk in the Players category, and Brian Burke in the Builders category. Here, NHL.com staff writer Tracey Myers profiles Curley. For Cindy Curley, hockey has been the gift that keeps on giving. The 62-year-old who grew up in Stow, Massachusetts, just outside of Boston, loves all the things that hockey brought her, not vice versa. "I never thought hockey owed me anything," she said. "I feel like it'll take me the rest of my life to pay back hockey for all the great opportunities and memories. It's a little surreal, honestly." Curley was one of the pioneers of the women's game, a forward who was part of those first world championship teams from the unofficial tournament in 1987 to the IIHF-sanctioned ones in the 1990s. It's why she is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto on Nov. 9. Curley won silver with the United States at the IIHF Women's World Championship in 1990, 1992 and 1994. Prior to that, she had 225 points (110 goals, 115 assists) in four seasons at Providence College, leading the Friars to Eastern College Athletic Conference championships in 1984 and 1985. items.title: Cutter Gauthier has hat trick in Ducks’ victory over Senators
items.body: ANAHEIM, Calif. — Cutter Gauthier had his second career hat trick, scoring the go-ahead goal early in the third period, and the Anaheim Ducks overcame a three-goal deficit to beat the Ottawa Senators 6-3 on Sunday night. Judd Caulfield scored twice, rookie Roger McQueen added another and Leo Carlsson had three assists to help the Ducks win for the second time in nine games. Anaheim went 4 for 5 on the power play. Laurent Brossoit made 20 saves in his Anaheim debut. Brossoit played his second NHL game in three seasons after being recalled from San Diego of the AHL on Saturday. Claude Giroux had a goal and an assist as the Senators lost for the third time on a five-game trip. Thomas Chabot and Michael Amadio also scored first-period goals while Jonas Johansson made 27 saves. After the Ducks rallied to tie it at 3 in the second period, they took advantage of a two-man advantage at 1:50 of the third when Gauthier scored from a sharp angle past Johansson. While still on a man advantage, Gauthier scored 36 seconds later for a two-goal cushion.

items.body: NEW YORK — It’s a loooong way from the Indiana Farmers Coliseum to Madison Square Garden. But on a Sunday night in Manhattan, after a career spent schlepping from Indianapolis, to Rockford, to Gothenburg, to Karlstad, to Tampa, to Syracuse and on to Bakersfield, Matt Tomkins walked out into the New York night with his fifth National Hockey League win, a 4-1 decision over the New York Rangers in his first start as an Edmonton Oiler. “It's been a long road, for sure,” said the 32-year-old journeyman, who cashed in his first NHL start since April of 2024. “It's been tough, but it's been enjoyable at the same time. items.title: McDavid becomes fastest player in NHL history to reach 30 assists in a season
items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid start to the season just keeps going. The Edmonton Oilers captain made NHL history on Sunday night, becoming the fastest player ever to hit 30 assists in a season. McDavid earned his 30th helper on Evan Bouchard's second-period power-play goal against the New York Rangers on Sunday night, hitting the milestone in just 15 games. Wayne Gretzky held the previous record, earning his 30th assist in his 16th game during the 1984-85 season. McDavid has earned at least one assist in all of the Oilers' games so far this season — a feat that broke an NHL record on Thursday with his 13th consecutive game with an assist. He's now up to 15 consecutive games. It's not just the helpers that are coming for McDavid — he's also been piling on the goals. In 15 games, the three-time Hart Trophy winner has nine goals and 39 points, on pace for 218 points over an 84-game season. The 30-year-old can continue to build on his record when the Oilers take on the Devils on Tuesday.
